steps.body: A missing length hides inside a whole: whole minus the known part reveals it, because the parts must rebuild the whole.
steps.narration: A missing length hides inside a whole: whole minus the known part reveals it, because the parts must rebuild the whole.

widget.prompt: Rebuild the whole: the known 40 m stretch is walked; hop the missing part's tens toward 75.

commonLandings.feedback: One ten of the missing stretch — keep walking until the whole is rebuilt.

widget.missFeedback: Each hop is 10. From 40, 3 hops land on 70.
widget.successFeedback: 70 — three tens of the missing part walked; five more meters would complete the 75 m whole.

predict.prompt: Whole 75, known part 40. The missing part must be…
predict.reveal: The parts rebuild the whole: 40 + 35 = 75, and no other missing part manages it.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g2p missing length.
invariants: Lengths compare only from a shared start, join by placing end to end, and split so the parts rebuild the whole exactly for g2p missing length.
misconceptions: Comparing unaligned ends, reading a ruler's end mark as a length, or letting a total drift from the sum of its parts.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What would have to change about the pieces for the total or the gap to come out differently?

widget.prompt: The whole trail runs 66 meters and the first stretch covers 36 meters. How many meters remain?

commonErrors.feedback: That stretched the trail LONGER — the remaining part is what the whole still owes after the first stretch.
Five meters of trail went missing; the parts must rebuild the whole exactly.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Line the lengths up: same starting point, then read what the ends say — joins add, gaps subtract.

widget.prompt: A drawing shows two bars: a 40 cm bar, and under it a 25 cm bar plus a mystery piece reaching the same end. What is the mystery piece?

options.label: The missing length: 40 − 25 = 15 cm
options.feedback: Correct — the two lower parts rebuild the 40 cm bar, so the mystery piece fills exactly the 15 cm gap.

options.label: The total: 40 + 25 = 65 cm
options.feedback: The bars END together, so they are equal — nothing in the drawing stacks to 65.

options.label: Another copy of the 25 cm piece
options.feedback: Two 25s would overshoot the 40 cm bar by 10 — the drawing's ends would no longer meet.

options.label: It cannot be found from a drawing
options.feedback: The drawing is exactly what makes it findable — equal ends turn the picture into an equation.
